sense: of money, for a common purpose

terms.gloss: a contribution of money, a collection
terms.comment: Each guest’s share of a dinner in Cicero; in the Vulgate the collection for the church at Jerusalem, and so the church collection. collēcta is also a gathering of people in Christian Latin (Jerome; Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a gift in small coin, alms, an offering
terms.comment: The small coins given to a god, a temple or a beggar; stipem cōnferre, to give to a collection. The nominative is not found.

phrases.latin: quoniam conlēctam ā convīvā, Crasse, exigis, nōn committam ut, sī dēfūgerim, tibi causam aliquam recūsandī dem
phrases.english: since you demand my share like a dinner guest’s, Crassus, I won’t back out and give you an excuse to refuse yours

phrases.latin: Dē collēctīs autem, quae fīunt in sānctōs
phrases.english: Now concerning the collection for the saints

sources: Lewis & Short: collecta · Lewis & Short: stips
Cicero checked against the Perseus Latin texts; the Vulgate against the Clementine text.
